# Rule catalog

All current rules emit warnings and have no automatic fix. A finding is a
review request, not proof of a failure. Spark-version targeting and measured
confidence tiers are not implemented.

| ID | Review topic |
| --- | --- |
| [TL001](TL001.md) | Potential driver-memory risk |
| [TL002](TL002.md) | Potential single-partition write bottleneck |
| [TL003](TL003.md) | Loop-carried withColumn() can grow the logical plan |

## TL001: Potential driver-memory risk

collect() and toPandas() materialize the entire result in driver memory. Whether it fits depends on result size, row width, and available memory.

**Review:** Keep the computation distributed, or explicitly limit the result if partial data is intended. If the full result is required, verify its memory footprint.

[Examples, evidence, and limitations](TL001.md).

## TL002: Potential single-partition write bottleneck

coalesce(1) reduces the input to one partition, limiting write parallelism. This can be intentional for small exports.

**Review:** Remove coalesce(1) or choose suitable partitioning for large outputs. Keep it only when a small, single-partition export is intentional.

[Examples, evidence, and limitations](TL002.md).

## TL003: Loop-carried withColumn() can grow the logical plan

Repeatedly assigning withColumn() back to the same DataFrame in a loop can build a large nested projection plan and increase planning overhead.

**Review:** Consider constructing the expressions together with select() or withColumns(). Preserve dependencies between columns; this is not a safe automatic rewrite.

[Examples, evidence, and limitations](TL003.md).
